ds: Fraudulent creation, sale or claiming of carbon credits and emissions allowances, including double counting, non-existent projects, inflated baselines, VAT fraud on allowance trading and misleading offset claims. Fraud harms climate goals and investors.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering from Environmental Crime (2021)
Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market, Core Carbon Principles (2023)
Europol, public material on emissions trading fraud
IOSCO, Voluntary Carbon Markets: Final Report (2024)

rat: Carbon credits and allowances traded via brokers and registries, sold to corporates and retail; credits are an asset outside the bank.

ind.n: Project lacking verifiable registry entry or independent verification
ind.cx: Credits sold from a project with no registry listing, uncertified verifier or conflicting documents.
ind.fp: New projects may still be in registration.
ind.ds: Credits sold from a project with no registry listing, uncertified verifier or conflicting documents.

ind.n: Same credits sold multiple times or retired and resold
ind.cx: Serial numbers appear in more than one transaction or after retirement.
ind.fp: Registry timing issues can show duplicate records.
ind.ds: Serial numbers appear in more than one transaction or after retirement.

ind.n: Credits priced far below or above market with no quality basis
ind.cx: Offers significantly diverge from benchmark prices for the project type.
ind.fp: Quality and vintage cause price variation.
ind.ds: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
ind.cn: Transaction price materially different from market value

ind.n: Intermediary or broker with no track record and aggressive marketing
ind.cx: New broker promises guaranteed returns or urgent allocation.
ind.ds: New broker promises guaranteed returns or urgent allocation.

ind.n: Round-trip trading and VAT fraud in allowance markets
ind.cx: Allowances bought and sold quickly among connected firms across borders with VAT unpaid.
ind.fp: Active traders turn over positions fast.
ind.ds: Funds or goods-linked payments loop back to the originator or between related counterparties, or are traded back and forth.
ind.cn: Circular or round-trip flows among related parties

ind.n: Funds routed to project developers in high-risk jurisdictions with no activity
ind.cx: Payments to developers in remote regions without site evidence.
ind.ds: Payments to developers in remote regions without site evidence.

ind.cx: Reduction claims implausible versus public data or comparable projects.
ind.ds: Reduction claims implausible versus public data or comparable projects.

ind.n: Retirement certificates claimed for corporate net-zero without registry proof
ind.cx: Companies or traders claim offsets via documents that do not match retirement records.
ind.fp: Delays between retirement and posting occur.
ind.ds: Companies or traders claim offsets via documents that do not match retirement records.

ctl.ds: Verifies credit serial numbers, status and retirement on recognised registries, checks verifier accreditation, host-country accounting and independent quality ratings, and uses technical review of claims. It prevents double counting and fraudulent environmental credits.

Requires end-user statements, authenticates their signatories, verifies licences and sites, and obtains post-delivery reports for goods and funds. It confirms that goods or funds reach the stated end use.

Uses satellite imagery, land-cover and site evidence to test claims about operations, land use, production or activity at a location. It provides independent physical verification that does not rely on counterparty documents.

Cross-checks asset ownership, title history, security registrations and registry changes against official registers, including for changes close to designation or transaction dates. It confirms that the person presenting an asset genuinely owns it.

ctl.n: Duplicate document and duplicate financing detection
ctl.ds: Hashes and fuzzy-matches invoice and shipping documents within and across clients and checks shared registries so one asset cannot be financed twice. It detects reused and fabricated paper.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.
Compares account flows with filed accounts, VAT or sales tax data and tax remittances, and links to VAT-fraud controls. It spots under-declared revenue and tax fraud proceeds.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.
Sets internal risk guidance, acceptance limits and approval levels for sectors, commodities and fundraising channels exposed to elevated risk. It gives consistent decisions on how far to engage.
